subject: Physics
topic: Newton's Laws of Motion & Momentum Systems
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Mechanics Conceptual Ontology, First-Move Atlas & Subtopic Competencies

stage_1_choose.name: System Demarcation & Frame Selection
invariants: Explicitly identify the physical body or closed multi-body system boundary.
Select reference frame (inertial ground frame vs accelerated non-inertial frame with explicit D'Alembert pseudo-forces).
Declare coordinate origin, positive axis orientation, and shared clock baseline (t = 0).
Register explicit model assumptions and idealizations before applying formulas.

stage_2_represent.name: Representation Construction
invariants: Translate physical story into an exact scientific representation before algebraic computation.
Allowed representation forms: Free-Body Diagram (FBD), Interaction Map, Coordinate/Trajectory Graph, Potential Well Curve, State Table, or Momentum Vector Triangle.
Typography floor: Every SVG diagram must declare text font-size >= 14px on all labels, coordinates, and annotations.
Visual integrity: Force vectors must originate at point of application/COM; action-reaction pairs must NEVER appear on the same isolated body.

stage_3_connect.name: Law Connection & Governing Constraints
invariants: Connect representation to the fundamental physical invariant law, never by guessing a formula name.
State explicit scope conditions: identify where the model holds and where it breaks.
Identify kinematic constraints: string inextensibility, rigid contact, shared time across orthogonal components.

stage_4_execute_and_check.name: Execution & Multi-Engine Physical Verification
invariants: Execute algebra step-by-step without skipping intermediate learner operations.
Sanity Check: Direction and sign must match physical reality.
Dimensional Homogeneity: Verify base SI dimensional powers [M]^a [L]^b [T]^c.
Dual Limiting Extremals: Stress-test at least 2 independent boundary conditions.
Cross-Core Recovery Anchor: Every distractor trap and reasoning step must link to an explicit numbered Core 1 atomic competency.

structural_pillars.name: Inertial Reference Frames & Motion as a State
structural_pillars.statement: An inertial frame is one in which Newton's 1st Law holds without fictitious forces. Motion is a state of velocity; net force determines acceleration (rate of change of velocity), not velocity itself.

structural_pillars.name: System Demarcation, Interaction Pairs & Isolated Systems
structural_pillars.statement: Forces are pairwise interactions between distinct bodies. Third-law pairs act on different bodies and never cancel on a single body's FBD. In an isolated multi-body system (net external impulse = 0), total momentum is strictly conserved.
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Closed system boundary demarcating internal from external interactions.

structural_pillars.name: Vector Addition, Orthogonal Decomposition & Motion Graphs
structural_pillars.statement: Forces add vectorially, not algebraically. Newton's 2nd Law holds independently along orthogonal axes. Velocity-time graph slopes represent acceleration, which multiplied by mass yields net force.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: \Sigma F_x = m a_x, \quad \Sigma F_y = m a_y, \quad F_{\text{net}} = m \frac{dv}{dt}
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Orthogonal Cartesian coordinate decomposition; piecewise differentiable kinematics.

structural_pillars.name: Newton II Dynamic Scaling & Two-Stage Stopping Models
structural_pillars.statement: Acceleration responds directly to net force and inversely to total system inertia. Stopping over distance or time requires coupling kinematic motion equations with dynamic force laws.
structural_pillars.mathematical_invariant: a = \frac{\Sigma F_{\text{ext}}}{M_{\text{tot}}}, \quad v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies F_{\text{stop}} = m|a| = \frac{m u^2}{2s}
structural_pillars.scope_condition: Constant mass systems; uniform stopping acceleration.

structural_pillars.name: Impulse-Momentum Theorem & Impact Duration Tradeoffs
structural_pillars.statement: Impulse equals total momentum change: J = Delta p = F_avg * Delta t. Spreading a fixed momentum change over a longer duration reduces peak contact force.

NLM-01.title: Motion is not Force
NLM-01.subtitle: Constant velocity can coexist with zero net force
NLM-01.canonical_rule: Constant velocity can coexist with zero net force; net force determines acceleration (rate of change of velocity), not velocity itself.
how_it_works: Choose the body and ask whether its velocity is changing.
Draw all external forces acting on that body.
Add them vectorially before discussing motion.
Check: zero net force means constant velocity, including rest.
subtopics: Zero net force coexisting with constant velocity
Distinction between zero net force and absence of individual forces
Inertial reference frames and the principle of inertia
Inertia during sudden braking (passenger lurch without fictitious forward force)
Coin tossed vertically in an accelerating train (horizontal velocity retention)
Fluid inertia in decelerating tankers (liquid surge toward front)
Motion on ideal frictionless surfaces requiring zero sustaining force
NLM-01.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming an object moving forward must have a net forward force pushing it.
NLM-01.worked_example: A crate moves right at 3 m/s while 60 N right and 60 N left act on it. Fnet = 0, so a = 0; it continues at constant velocity.

guided_try.prompt: A puck glides at constant velocity on an ideal frictionless surface. What horizontal net force is required?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.

NLM-01.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example (direction, mass, force, time, or system boundary). Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-01.watch_out: A moving object does not automatically need a forward net force.

NLM-02.title: Choose the Body Before Drawing Forces
NLM-02.subtitle: Interactions become forces only after the body is chosen
NLM-02.canonical_rule: Interactions become forces only after the target body is chosen; only external forces acting ON the chosen body enter Sigma F = ma.
NLM-02.scope_condition: Closed system boundary demarcating internal from external interactions.
how_it_works: Circle the body/system being analysed.
List interacting bodies: Earth, surface, rope, hand, etc.
Convert each interaction into one force arrow on the chosen body.
Do not include forces the chosen body exerts on something else.
subtopics: Closed system boundary demarcation
Interaction mapping: identifying contact vs non-contact external agents
Naming convention: 'force on X by Y'
Eliminating body confusion (never placing forces exerted BY the body on its own FBD)
FBD construction for isolated bodies
Ideal frictionless surfaces: normal contact force only, zero shear
NLM-02.easy_mistake_to_make: Drawing forces exerted BY the body onto its own Free-Body Diagram.
NLM-02.worked_example: For a book on a table, the book FBD contains Earth-on-book weight and table-on-book normal. The book-on-table force belongs to the table FBD.

guided_try.prompt: A crate is pushed by a worker while sliding on a floor. Name three possible external interactions on the crate.
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.

NLM-02.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-02.watch_out: An interaction pair is not automatically two arrows on one FBD.

NLM-03.title: Net Force is a Vector Sum
NLM-03.subtitle: Balanced forces and no forces are different statements
NLM-03.canonical_rule: Forces add vectorially, not algebraically; balanced forces produce zero acceleration along each orthogonal axis independently.
NLM-03.scope_condition: Orthogonal Cartesian coordinate decomposition (Sigma F_x = m a_x, Sigma F_y = m a_y).
how_it_works: Choose +x and +y.
Resolve forces into components when needed.
Compute Sigma Fx and Sigma Fy.
Only then infer acceleration components.
subtopics: Collinear vector addition with explicit signed components
Orthogonal Cartesian force decomposition (Sigma F_x = m a_x, Sigma F_y = m a_y)
Dynamic equilibrium at constant velocity (horse pulling cart at constant speed)
Distinguishing balanced forces from absence of forces
Mass as the quantitative measure of translational inertia
Ranking inertia across equal-volume or differing-mass objects
NLM-03.easy_mistake_to_make: Adding vector magnitudes directly without trigonometric component resolution.
NLM-03.worked_example: A cart has 25 N right and 10 N left. With right positive, Fnet,x = 25 - 10 = 15 N right.

guided_try.prompt: A box has 30 N right and 30 N left. What is its horizontal acceleration?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
guided_try.solution: Answer: 0 m/s^2, regardless of its current velocity.

NLM-03.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-03.watch_out: Do not confuse 'Fnet = 0' with 'there are no forces.'

NLM-04.title: Newton II and Scaling
NLM-04.subtitle: Acceleration responds to net force and mass together
NLM-04.canonical_rule: Acceleration is directly proportional to net force and inversely proportional to total mass: a = Sigma F_ext / M_tot.
NLM-04.scope_condition: Constant mass systems (non-relativistic, non-rocket mass shedding).
how_it_works: Find Fnet from the FBD.
Read or calculate the mass in kilograms.
Use a = Fnet / m.
For scaling, form the ratio (F2/F1) / (m2/m1).
subtopics: Fundamental dynamic equation: F_net = ma
Force and mass scaling ratios: a2/a1 = (F2/F1)(m1/m2)
Coupled masses under the same external force: a_tot = (a1 * a2)/(a1 + a2)
Single-body vs multi-body composite system acceleration
Atwood machine coupled acceleration and string tension harmonic mean
NLM-04.easy_mistake_to_make: Using individual applied force instead of vector net force in a = F/m.
NLM-04.worked_example: If force doubles while mass triples, a_new / a_old = 2 / 3.

guided_try.prompt: The same force accelerates mass A at 6 m/s^2 and mass B at 3 m/s^2. If they are tied together, what is the acceleration?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.

NLM-04.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-04.watch_out: Mass in the denominator means larger mass gives smaller acceleration for the same net force.

NLM-05.title: Stopping Force Needs Two Models
NLM-05.subtitle: Kinematics supplies acceleration; Newton II supplies force
NLM-05.canonical_rule: Determining stopping force requires coupling kinematics with dynamics: kinematics supplies acceleration; Newton II supplies retarding force.
NLM-05.scope_condition: Uniform stopping acceleration over displacement s or duration t.
how_it_works: Write the motion state: u, v = 0, s.
Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as to find a.
Use F = ma with sign/direction explicit.
If time is requested, use v = u + at.
subtopics: Two-stage model coupling: Kinematics <-> Dynamics
Stopping over distance s: v^2 = u^2 + 2as => a = -u^2/(2s)
Stopping force calculation: F_stop = m|a| = mu^2/(2s)
Stopping duration: v = u + at => t = u/|a| = 2s/u
Quadratic velocity scaling of stopping force
NLM-05.easy_mistake_to_make: Attempting to calculate stopping force without determining acceleration or time.
NLM-05.worked_example: A 0.020 kg pellet at 100 m/s stops uniformly in 0.10 m. a = (0 - 10000) / 0.20 = -50000 m/s^2, so F = -1000 N.

guided_try.prompt: If the same pellet stops over twice the distance, what happens to |a| and |F|?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.

NLM-05.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-05.watch_out: Do not skip the acceleration step when distance is given.

NLM-06.title: Momentum is a Signed State
NLM-06.subtitle: Momentum carries the direction of velocity
NLM-06.canonical_rule: Momentum p = m * v is a directional vector carrying the sign of velocity; reversing direction produces Delta p = -m(v1 + v2), not zero.
how_it_works: Choose a positive direction.
Write signed velocities.
Convert to signed momenta.
Subtract final minus initial: Delta p = p_f - p_i.
subtopics: Linear momentum as signed vector quantity: p = mv
1D coordinate sign assignment (+p and -p)
Rebound dynamics: reversal of velocity producing large Delta p
Directional momentum change vs scalar speed difference
Momentum-velocity (p-v) graph slope as mass m
Momentum-mass (p-m) graph slope as velocity v
NLM-06.easy_mistake_to_make: Subtracting momentum magnitudes without accounting for opposite directional signs.
NLM-06.worked_example: A 0.20 kg ball changes from +8 m/s to -6 m/s. Delta p = 0.20(-6) - 0.20(8) = -2.8 kg m/s.

guided_try.prompt: At fixed mass, what is the shape of a p-v graph?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
guided_try.solution: Answer: A straight line through the origin with slope equal to mass m.

NLM-06.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-06.watch_out: Rebounding doubles roughly the momentum change compared to just stopping.

NLM-07.title: Impulse and Average Force
NLM-07.subtitle: The same momentum change can be spread over more time
NLM-07.canonical_rule: Impulse J = Delta p = F_avg * Delta t; spreading a fixed momentum change over a longer time interval reduces the peak contact force.
how_it_works: Find the signed Delta p.
Identify the interaction duration Delta t.
Divide Delta p by Delta t to obtain F_avg.
Check sign: force direction matches Delta p.
subtopics: Impulse-momentum theorem: J = Delta p = F_avg * Delta t
Impact duration tradeoff: extending Delta t reduces average force
Catching mechanics: cushioning impact by moving hands backward
Force-time (F-t) graph: area under curve equals total impulse Delta p
Distinguishing impulse (N*s) from work (J) and momentum from force
NLM-07.easy_mistake_to_make: Confusing impulse (change in momentum in N*s) with work done (energy transferred in Joules).
NLM-07.worked_example: A 0.50 kg ball at +12 m/s stops in 0.30 s: Delta p = -6 kg m/s, F_avg = -20 N.

guided_try.prompt: If the same ball is stopped in twice the time, what happens to average force magnitude?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.

NLM-07.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-07.watch_out: Moving hands backward while catching increases Delta t, reducing F_avg.

NLM-08.title: Newton III Pairs
NLM-08.subtitle: Equal and opposite does not mean same body
NLM-08.canonical_rule: Every interaction between two bodies consists of equal and opposite forces acting simultaneously on different bodies: F_12 = -F_21.
NLM-08.scope_condition: Universal interaction law valid across all mass ratios and contact/field interfaces.
how_it_works: Name both interacting bodies.
Write the two force names: 'force on B by A' and 'force on A by B'.
Place each force on the correct body's FBD.
Use Newton II separately to compare accelerations.
subtopics: Third-law reciprocal action-reaction pairs: F_AB = -F_BA
Forces acting on strictly different bodies: never cancelling on one body's FBD
Normal force vs weight distinction on a resting body (balanced forces on one body vs 3rd law pair)
Wall push reaction force
Horse and cart paradox resolution via ground friction on horse hooves
Sprinkler rotational reaction via backward fluid ejection
NLM-08.easy_mistake_to_make: Believing a massive object exerts a greater gravitational or contact force than a lighter object.
NLM-08.worked_example: Earth pulls an apple downward with the same force magnitude that the apple pulls Earth upward. Their accelerations differ because their masses differ.

guided_try.prompt: What is the third-law partner of the table-on-book normal force?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.

NLM-08.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-08.watch_out: Normal and weight on a book are not a third-law pair; they act on the same body.

NLM-09.title: Momentum Conservation is a System Statement
NLM-09.subtitle: Choose the system and check external impulse first
NLM-09.canonical_rule: In the absence of net external impulse (Sigma F_ext = 0), the total momentum of a multi-body system is strictly conserved: P_total = const.
NLM-09.scope_condition: Isolated multi-body systems; internal interaction forces cancel identically by Newton III.
how_it_works: Draw a system boundary.
Choose a positive direction.
List all system bodies before and after.
Equate total initial and final momentum along the axis.
subtopics: System boundary demarcation and internal force cancellation
External impulse verification condition: Sigma F_ext = 0
Why a falling ball alone does not conserve momentum (external gravity impulse)
Why the ball + Earth system conserves total momentum
Separation from rest: P_initial = 0 => m1*v1 + m2*v2 = 0
Two skaters pushing apart on frictionless ice
NLM-09.easy_mistake_to_make: Applying momentum conservation to an isolated single body under external gravity.
NLM-09.worked_example: Two skaters push apart from rest. For the two-skater system, initial total p = 0, so their final momenta are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

guided_try.prompt: A falling ball speeds up under gravity. Is the ball-only momentum conserved?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
guided_try.solution: Answer: No; gravity exerts an external impulse on the ball.

NLM-09.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-09.watch_out: Always check external impulse before writing p_initial = p_final.

NLM-10.title: Recoil, Rockets and Exchanged Momentum
NLM-10.subtitle: Equal momentum can mean very different speeds
NLM-10.canonical_rule: In recoil and separation events, internal momentum exchange produces equal and opposite momenta, with speeds scaling inversely with mass.
NLM-10.scope_condition: Isolated explosive or recoil events; rocket mass expulsion.
how_it_works: Choose launcher + projectile (or rocket + exhaust) as the system.
Set initial total momentum.
Assign opposite signs after separation.
Solve for the unknown velocity; check kinetic energy ratio K2/K1 = m1/m2.
subtopics: Recoil dynamics in isolated systems: m_bullet * v_bullet = m_gun * v_recoil
Inverse speed-mass scaling: v proportional to 1/m for equal momentum
Kinetic energy partitioning: K = p^2/(2m) proportional to 1/m (lighter object carries most kinetic energy)
Rocket propulsion in deep space via backward exhaust ejection
Thrust via continuous mass ejection rate: F_thrust = v_rel * (dm/dt)
NLM-10.easy_mistake_to_make: Assuming equal momentum implies equal speed or equal kinetic energy.
NLM-10.worked_example: A 0.020 kg bullet leaves a 2.0 kg pistol at +150 m/s from rest. 0 = (0.020)(150) + 2*v, so v = -1.5 m/s.

guided_try.prompt: Two rifles fire identical bullets with the same bullet momentum. Which rifle has larger recoil speed?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.
guided_try.solution: Answer: The lighter rifle (since v_recoil = p / m_rifle).

NLM-10.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-10.watch_out: The lighter body always carries away the majority of kinetic energy: K = p^2 / (2m).

NLM-11.title: Read Force from a Motion Graph
NLM-11.subtitle: v-t slope -> acceleration -> force
NLM-11.canonical_rule: The slope of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration (dv/dt), which multiplied by mass yields net force: F_net = m * (dv/dt).
how_it_works: Read two points on the straight segment.
Compute a = Delta v / Delta t.
Convert mass to kilograms.
Apply F = ma and interpret the sign (retardation vs acceleration).
subtopics: Velocity-time graph slope as acceleration: a = Delta v / Delta t
Net force deduction: F_net = m * slope
Frictional retarding force deduction from deceleration slope
Segmented piecewise velocity-time profiles
Avoiding area misinterpretation (area under v-t is displacement, not force)
NLM-11.easy_mistake_to_make: Inferring force from the height of the velocity curve rather than its slope.
NLM-11.worked_example: A 50 g object slows from 80 m/s to 0 in 8 s. a = -10 m/s^2; F = 0.050 * (-10) = -0.50 N.

guided_try.prompt: If the same velocity change takes twice as long, what happens to |a| and |F|?
guided_try.guide: Name the body/system -> draw the representation -> state the law before calculating.

NLM-11.faded_try: Change one feature of the worked example. Which parts of the reasoning remain valid and which must change?
NLM-11.watch_out: Do not confuse graph height (velocity) with graph slope (acceleration).

first_move_atlas.first_physics_move: draw only forces on that body
Delta p then Delta p/Delta t
force on B by A <-> force on A by B
check external impulse, then conserve total p
lighter mass -> larger speed for same |p|
a = Delta v / Delta t then F=ma

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A sustained net force is required to keep a body in constant velocity.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Zero net force maintains constant velocity (Newton's 1st Law). Forces are only required to change velocity (accelerate).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: If Action equals Reaction, they must cancel each other out, making acceleration impossible.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Action and Reaction act on strictly distinct bodies. Acceleration of any single body depends only on forces acting ON that body.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Normal reaction N always equals mg.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Normal force is an adjusting constraint force: on an incline N = mg cos theta; in an accelerating elevator N = m(g +- a).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Friction always acts in the direction opposite to the object's velocity in the lab frame.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Friction opposes relative motion between contacting surfaces. It can accelerate an object forward (e.g. car drive wheels, walking, crate on accelerating truck bed).

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Stopping an object transfers more momentum than having it bounce back at the same speed.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Momentum is a signed state vector. Rebounding reverses direction, producing Delta p = -m(v1 + v2), roughly double the momentum change of merely stopping.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: In a rifle-bullet explosion, equal momenta mean equal kinetic energy and equal destructiveness.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Kinetic energy K = p^2 / (2m). For equal momentum magnitudes, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass: the light bullet absorbs almost all explosive energy.
